archetype.name: Fringe Contender (shootout offense)
archetype.definition: A top-six offense paired with the league's worst defense. Detroit is good enough to beat anyone and porous enough to lose to anyone, so its 2-2 record and slightly negative point differential are an honest summary of its play.

report.headline: Elite Goff offense, league-worst defense: every Lions game is a track meet
report.take:
Detroit's offense looks like the 2024 version again. Its 0.144 EPA per play ranks 6th, nearly matching the 0.155 of that 15-win season, and the passing game is the engine: 4th in pass EPA and 3rd in success rate. Jared Goff is averaging about 303 passing yards a game. St. Brown, LaPorta, Gibbs and Williams split a deep target tree, so there is no single coverage answer. The offense has scored 31, 31, 31 and 26, and it has turned the ball over once in four games.

The problem is everything on the other side. The Lions allow 0.203 EPA per play, last in the league. That is essentially the 0.207 of the 2020 team that finished 30th in net EPA. They are 30th against the pass, 29th against the run, last on deep balls, last on third down and 31st in red-zone touchdown rate. Opponents have averaged roughly 327 passing yards a game. This isn't sloppiness: Detroit ranks 1st in missed-tackle rate. It is coverage getting beaten over the top, and the injury report explains a lot of it. Brian Branch has not played. Thomas Harper is on IR. Rock Ya-Sin is doubtful this week.

The numbers flatter the defense in two places, and that should worry fans more than it does. First, the turnover margin is +0.8 per game, 5th in the league, and Detroit is still being outscored. Strip out that margin and this is a losing team on the field. Second, the 15 sacks (2nd) come from only a 15th-ranked pressure rate, which means the rush is converting pressure into sacks at a rate that rarely holds. The defense is getting real help in both areas and is still last.

The market hasn't caught up. Detroit is 0-3-1 against the spread despite being favored in three of its four games, and all four games went over the total by an average of about 10 points. The opponent defenses help explain the offense: New Orleans and Buffalo currently rank 30th and 29th. The schedule ahead flips that. Minnesota's top-ranked defense appears twice, and Chicago and Tampa Bay both rank 5th. In exchange, Detroit's defense will face a run of bottom-ten offenses. Expect the scores to come down from here, with the Lions' fate depending on how fast the secondary gets healthy.

strengths.title: A passing game near its 2024 peak
strengths.body: Detroit is 4th in pass EPA and 3rd in overall success rate, and Goff has produced positive passing EPA in every game, including an 18.6 at Buffalo. The target spread across four reliable options and a line ranked 8th in pressure rate allowed make this sustainable. It matches the 2024 offense in the history rather than being a hot streak.

strengths.title: A pass rush that finishes
strengths.body: Fifteen sacks through four games ranks 2nd, with a 6th-ranked sack rate, and two five-sack games. It is the one part of the defense that wins downs. But with only the 15th-best pressure rate behind it, the conversion rate from pressure to sack is unusually high and should cool toward the middle of the pack.

strengths.title: Clean ball security and special teams
strengths.body: Detroit has one giveaway in four games, which drives most of the +0.8 turnover margin. Special teams add 2.75 EPA a game, 6th in the league. The special-teams value is fairly stable. A one-turnover pace will not last, but Goff's offense has not been turnover-prone, so the margin should drift down rather than collapse.

concerns.title: The defense loses the big plays
concerns.body: The Lions are last in EPA allowed and last on deep passes, 26th in explosive pass rate and 31st in explosive run rate. They also fail to get off the field: last on third down and 31st in the red zone. Tackling is not the issue, since they rank 1st in missed-tackle rate. Coverage is. With Branch yet to play, Harper on IR into November and Ya-Sin hurt, it is partly an injury story and should improve, but 2020 is the reminder that it can stay this bad.

concerns.title: Losing the scoreboard despite winning turnovers
concerns.body: A +0.8 turnover margin usually buys a positive point differential. Detroit is still -2 per game, with net EPA ranked 18th. When the takeaways and the one-giveaway pace normalize, the underlying team is roughly .500 or worse unless the defense improves. The 0-3-1 record against the spread says the market keeps pricing the offense and ignoring the other side.

concerns.title: Run game thinning with the interior line
concerns.body: Blockers are giving Gibbs room early: 3.04 yards before contact ranks 4th. But a 29th-ranked stuff rate and negative run EPA say too many runs die at the line. Rushing yards have fallen from 165 to 46 by week four. Starting guard Ben Bartch is out and center Cade Mays is on IR until roughly Week 7, so expect more of a pass-only offense in the short term.

trend.note: Wins and losses have alternated, but the game is the same every week: 26-31 points scored and 24-41 allowed, with all four games going over. The only real movement is a fading run game, from 165 rushing yards in Week 1 to 46 in Week 4, as the interior line got hurt.

nextGame.headline: Goff's passing game meets a bottom-two pass defense
nextGame.body:
Arizona's defense is built backwards for this matchup. It is 5th against the run but 31st in pass EPA allowed, 31st in explosive pass rate and 30th on deep throws. That is exactly where Detroit wants to live, especially with the run game stuffed and a guard out. On the other side, the Cardinals' offense is middling (17th) and passes poorly under Jacoby Brissett (23rd in pass EPA). That makes them a weaker test of Detroit's secondary than Buffalo or Carolina were. Arizona's run success rate ranks 6th, though, and it controls the clock (6th in time of possession), so it can shorten the game against Detroit's 29th-ranked run defense.

The availability edge leans Detroit. Arizona lost left tackle Paris Johnson Jr., a 100%-snap starter, for the season. Guard Isaiah Adams and running back Jeremiyah Love are questionable, and Detroit's 2nd-ranked sack total gets a thinner protection front to attack. Detroit is missing starting guard Ben Bartch and likely Ya-Sin at corner, with Harper on IR. Branch's return, which Campbell called close, is the biggest swing for a defense that has nothing behind its starters.

keyMatchups.title: Detroit air attack vs Arizona coverage
keyMatchups.body: Detroit is 4th in pass EPA and Arizona is 31st in pass EPA allowed. Arizona also ranks 31st on short passes and 30th on deep ones, so there is no part of the field it protects. This is the clearest mismatch on the board and should hold regardless of game script.

keyMatchups.title: Lions rush vs a replacement left tackle
keyMatchups.body: Detroit's pass rush converts at a top-six sack rate. Arizona just lost its every-snap left tackle and has a guard questionable. Sacks are Detroit's only reliable drive-killer, and this is a good spot for them.

keyMatchups.title: Cardinals' ground game and the clock
keyMatchups.body: Arizona's 6th-ranked run success rate against Detroit's 29th-ranked run defense is the Cardinals' path to keeping Goff on the sideline and covering. If Love sits, much of that threat goes with him.

nextGame.watch: Whether Brian Branch plays. A depleted Lions secondary without Ya-Sin and Harper is the only thing that makes Brissett dangerous.

restOfSeason.body:
The offense is the real part of this team. Its history and four steady games back it up. But the schedule toughens on that side: Minnesota's top-ranked defense twice, Chicago twice, and Tampa Bay and Atlanta, all top-eight defenses. Thirty points a game becomes high-20s. The defense should improve from historically bad to merely bad. Part of that is the return of Branch now and Harper around November 1. Part is a slate full of weak offenses: Minnesota 28th, Miami 30th, Tampa Bay 32nd, Tennessee and Green Bay 26th.

What will regress: the turnover margin, the pressure-to-sack conversion and the run of overs. What should hold: the passing game and special teams. Six division games, four of them against teams currently ahead of or level with Detroit, will decide whether this is a nine-win wild-card bubble team or another 2025-style finish.
swingFactors: Branch and Harper returning to the secondary
Interior line health (Bartch, Mays) and the run game
Turnover margin normalizing from +0.8 a game

bets.reason: All four Detroit games have gone over, averaging 61.5 combined points. Blending each side's scoring and points allowed lands around 56. Arizona's 31st-ranked pass defense and Detroit's 32nd-ranked defense overall are the reason. The number is already high, which keeps this a lean.

The line implies roughly 29.5 for Detroit, which has scored 31 in three of four games. Its 4th-ranked passing game faces a defense that is 31st against the pass and 30th on deep balls. The Bartch absence pushes Detroit even further toward passing, which is exactly where Arizona is weak.

Detroit is 0-3-1 against the spread and failed to cover all three times it was favored, because its last-ranked defense keeps opponents in games. Arizona can run (6th in run success) against a 29th-ranked run defense and controls the clock. A road favorite of more than a field goal is asking too much of this defense.

confidence.note: Four games is a small sample, but the profile is consistent week to week and lines up with known secondary injuries.
